chunks: And by his chain, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you.'
He said: 'That which you intend to contract upon him. Do not say,
And regarding His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Contract with them if you know any good in them.'
He said: 'The good is if you know that he has wealth.'

key_terms.إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا: if you know good in them

ai.seo_question: How should a master determine the payment for a slave's freedom contract according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of Surah An-Nur 24:33 regarding mukataba (contracted slavery). He interprets 'wealth of Allah' as the master's intended deduction, advising that the master should pay the servant the full amount he plans to keep, rather than a fixed sum, thereby ensuring generosity. Furthermore, he defines the condition of 'knowing good' in the verse as the servant's actual possession of wealth to fulfill the contract.
